lens: World-model / agentic AI for motor biosignals — reframe the trained S-JEPA as a world model of body movement: latent next-state prediction, predictive surprise / anomaly scoring, latent rollouts (imagined futures), and a concrete path toward action/goal conditioning for assistive robotics and neurorehabilitation closed loops.
title: Imagining the Next Step: Reframing a Skeleton JEPA as a World Model of Gait via Latent Future Prediction and Predictive Surprise
one_sentence_question: Can a Skeleton JEPA trained only to infill same-clip, spatially masked joints be repurposed without retraining as a world model that forecasts future body state in latent space, and does its per-condition prediction error (predictive surprise) rank motor conditions under strict source-video grouping?
why_novel: The JEPA-as-world-model literature (LeCun 2022) argues JEPA predicts in representation space and should therefore support planning and forward simulation, and I-JEPA (CVPR 2023), V-JEPA (2024), MC-JEPA, A-JEPA and H-JEPA operationalize latent prediction for vision and embodied/robot action. None of them treat a JEPA trained on human skeleton pose as a world model of movement, nor use its latent prediction error as a motor biosignal. This project's S-JEPA was trained ONLY for cross-joint spatial infilling with full bidirectional temporal access — the internals doc states explicitly it is 'not forecasting future frames.' The novel move is a zero-shot probe that flips the mask axis: hide FUTURE time segments (all 33 joints) rather than joints, and ask the frozen predictor to imagine the next body state. This cleanly tests the world-model thesis on the motor side, and BOTH outcomes are a genuine contribution: if it forecasts, latent forward dynamics emerged implicitly from an infilling objective; if it fails, we establish a sharp empirical boundary (infilling ≠ forecasting) that the JEPA-as-world-model literature currently assumes away, motivating causal temporal/action-conditioned JEPA (A-JEPA / H-JEPA style) for biosignals. The predictive-surprise scoring additionally links foundation-model SSL to predictive-processing / active-inference accounts of motor control (surprise as a feedback signal), which the workshop's motor-loop emphasis invites but which no prior submission on this corpus supplies.
workshop_fit: Direct hit on the 2026 edition's stated emphasis on 'the motor side of the loop' (movement, motor control, closed-loop interaction) and 'scaling/generalization techniques from robotics and embodied AI into biosignal modeling.' It maps onto four named topics: foundation models for movement/motor control, embodied intelligence and sensorimotor representation learning, SSL for biosignals (pose-from-video is an explicit behavioral biosignal), and interpretability/evaluation of biosignal representations (predictive surprise as an interpretable probe). The future-state prediction, rollout, and goal-conditioning narrative is the exact embodied-AI framing the CFP solicits, while remaining grounded in the existing frozen checkpoints.

decisive_experiments.name: Zero-shot latent future-state prediction (temporal masking) on frozen checkpoints
decisive_experiments.question: Does a predictor trained for same-clip cross-joint infilling transfer to forecasting future body state in latent space?
decisive_experiments.method: For each prepared sequence (64 frames -> 16 segments x 33 joints = 528 tokens), build a temporal target_mask hiding ALL 33 joints in the last h in {2,4,8} segments; run view_encoder with keep_mask=~target_mask (past-only context), scatter past features + learned mask tokens through the frozen SkeletonPredictor, and gather the EMA target encoder's latents at the same future positions from the FULL clip. Compare against (a) the in-distribution spatial-infilling mask at matched M (joint-wise, all-time; spot-check reports mean cosine 0.574 on 114 tokens/seq) as a same-clip ceiling, and (b) a trivial 'copy last past-segment latent' baseline.
decisive_experiments.metric: Per-token cosine similarity (and surprise = 1 - cosine) at future positions, aggregated per sequence and per joint; error-vs-horizon curve.
decisive_experiments.expected_if_world_model: Future cosine > 0 and above the copy baseline at h=2, decaying monotonically with horizon (compounding error), approaching but below the spatial-infilling ceiling.
decisive_experiments.null_outcome: Future cosine ~ 0 / no better than copy baseline at any horizon -> the predictor has no latent forward dynamics; infilling ≠ forecasting (clean, publishable negative).
decisive_experiments.runtime: Seconds-to-minutes; checkpoints (all 5 stages + final) and pose caches are already on disk, no training.

decisive_experiments.name: Predictive-surprise condition scoring under strict source-video grouping
decisive_experiments.question: Is future-state prediction error structured by movement condition, or by nuisance variables?
decisive_experiments.method: Compute per-sequence surprise from E1 (h=4 headline, with h sensitivity), then aggregate by condition. Report condition-wise median surprise and pairwise AUROC (normal vs each abnormal; abnormal-vs-abnormal) with bootstrap CIs resampled at the VIDEO level (35 videos, not 159 sequences) to avoid pseudoreplication. Run two mandatory controls: (1) missingness-only surprise (surprise from a missingness-feature linear model, matching the missingness-only lane that already hits 0.448 acc on all-96) and (2) provenance control (canonical 96 vs augmented-normal 63 path).
decisive_experiments.metric: Condition-ranked median surprise; normal-vs-condition AUROC with video-level bootstrap CIs; partial-out of missingness/provenance.
decisive_experiments.expected_if_world_model: Monotonic surprise ordering normal < Parkinson's ~ stroke < myopathic < cerebral-palsy (or a defensible severity order), surviving the missingness and provenance controls.
decisive_experiments.null_outcome: Surprise tracks missingness or acquisition path (canonical vs augmented) rather than condition — indistinguishable from the 0.448 missingness-only baseline.
decisive_experiments.runtime: Minutes; pure frozen-checkpoint scoring plus bootstrap.

decisive_experiments.name: Raw-coordinate kinematic world-model baseline in a matched metric
decisive_experiments.question: Does the latent world model add anything over a kinematic extrapolator, given raw coords already trivially solve some tasks (laterality raw R2 ~ 1.0 vs learned -0.187)?
decisive_experiments.method: Constant-velocity and zero-velocity (carry-last-frame) extrapolation of the last h segments in normalized coordinates. Report (a) coordinate error per body scale, and (b) encode the extrapolated future through the frozen target encoder to measure latent distance to the true future latent — the SAME latent metric as E1 — then re-rank conditions head-to-head against JEPA surprise.
decisive_experiments.metric: Coordinate error (normalized) and kinematic-latent surprise; head-to-head condition ranking and AUROC vs JEPA surprise.
decisive_experiments.expected_if_world_model: JEPA latent surprise ranks conditions at least as well as, or better than, kinematic extrapolation, with a compactness/interpretability advantage (one 96-d latent metric).
decisive_experiments.null_outcome: Constant-velocity extrapolation already ranks conditions equally or better -> JEPA adds nothing (honest negative consistent with the laterality precedent).

decisive_experiments.name: Source-disjoint retraining for an honest generalization estimate
decisive_experiments.question: Is the surprise-ranking a real signal, or a transductive artifact of video identity?
decisive_experiments.method: GroupKFold by source video (or leave-one-video-out given 35 videos) retrain the encoder with held-out source videos excluded — single-stage normal or the full curriculum — then recompute E1–E2 surprise on held-out videos only. Report the transductive-vs-held-out gap and fold variance. This is the ONLY valid generalization estimate per the audit's transductivity rule.
decisive_experiments.metric: Held-out surprise ranking and AUROC; transductive-vs-held-out gap; per-fold CIs.
decisive_experiments.expected_if_world_model: Surprise ranking survives (attenuated) on held-out videos -> signal generalizes past the training videos.
decisive_experiments.null_outcome: Ranking collapses on held-out videos (video identity / provenance dominates); folds are tiny (1 canonical normal video, 2 Parkinson's, 2 CP) so variance is high — report as a pilot, not a benchmark.
decisive_experiments.runtime: The only training cost: full 600-epoch curriculum ~20 min on this machine, single-stage folds a few minutes each; 2-5 folds fit comfortably in the 3-day window.

decisive_experiments.name: Autoregressive latent rollouts + goal/action-conditioning pilot (path to closed loop)
decisive_experiments.question: Can the predictor be used for 'imagined futures' and steered by a goal/action signal — the seed of a motor closed loop?
decisive_experiments.method: (a) Open-loop rollout: predict the next h segments' latents, feed the predicted latents back as context, recurse k steps; measure divergence from teacher-forced rollout (error growth, collapse to the condition mean). (b) Goal/action-conditioning feasibility: append a conditioning token (a goal end-posture latent, or a scalar cadence/speed signal) to the predictor grid and test whether the rollout is pulled toward the goal (optionally a tiny predictor-only fine-tune; encoder stays frozen).
decisive_experiments.metric: Rollout-vs-teacher divergence vs step; goal-directed displacement of the rollout endpoint toward the goal posture.
decisive_experiments.expected_if_world_model: Bounded, compounding divergence (no immediate collapse) and a measurable goal-pull -> evidence the latent dynamics are controllable, motivating an action-conditioned world model for assistive robotics / neurorehab.
decisive_experiments.null_outcome: Rollout collapses to the condition mean within a few steps and the goal token has no effect -> motivates explicit temporal/action-conditioned JEPA training (A-JEPA/H-JEPA style) as the natural next project.
decisive_experiments.runtime: Feasibility pilot (hours); if it does not fit the deadline, it is honestly labeled future work in the 5-page paper.

effort_and_feasibility: Very high. Experiments E1–E3 are pure frozen-checkpoint probes: the five stage checkpoints plus the final curriculum checkpoint, prepared pose caches (poses/ and poses_augmented/), and the self-contained classes (SkeletonPatchEncoder, SkeletonPredictor, SJEPAGait, prepare_sequence, uniform_neurologic_mask) are all already on disk, so each probe is seconds-to-minutes. E4 is the only training, and the audit records a full 600-epoch curriculum at ~20 min on this machine with single-stage retrains of a few minutes, so 2-5 source-disjoint folds fit easily before Sep 5 AoE. E5 is a feasibility pilot or clearly labeled future work. The whole direction is executable within the 3-day window with substantial time left to write, run controls, and iterate the 5 pages.
main_risks: Predictor trained for infilling, not forecasting: bidirectional attention and same-clip targets mean temporal future-masking is out-of-distribution for the predictor; it may fail to forecast at all (cosine ~ 0). This is the central null and must be framed as a result, not hidden.

Transductivity: the frozen encoder saw all 35 source videos, so any generalization claim requires the E4 source-disjoint retrain; with 1 canonical normal video, 2 Parkinson's, and 2 CP videos the folds are tiny and high-variance — a pilot, not a benchmark.

Provenance/missingness confound: 63/75 normal training rows come from the added extraction path and missingness-only features already reach 0.448 acc on all-96, so surprise may track acquisition path or missingness rather than condition; the E2 controls are mandatory.

Kinematic ceiling: raw coordinates trivially solve some tasks (laterality raw R2 ~ 1.0 vs learned -0.187), so a constant-velocity extrapolation baseline may already rank conditions and leave no JEPA advantage — a real, reportable null.

Metric ambiguity: cosine vs MSE vs the training softmax-CE on the 96-d EMA-target latent are not interchangeable and may rank conditions differently; the surprise metric must be pre-registered before results are inspected.

Small data / single seed: 159 sequences from 35 videos with no seed replication means condition-level surprise distributions overlap heavily and any 'ranking' is descriptive, not a validated clinical biomarker.
paper_outline_5p: P1 (Intro + positioning): state the JEPA-as-world-model thesis (LeCun 2022) and how I-JEPA/V-JEPA/MC-JEPA/A-JEPA realize latent prediction for vision and embodied action; identify the gap — no one treats a skeleton JEPA as a world model of movement or uses its prediction error as a motor biosignal; give the one-sentence question and three contributions. P2 (Method): recap the S-JEPA (encoder/predictor/EMA target, joint-wise masking over 12 authorized joints, 528 tokens, same-clip objective) and introduce the reframe — temporal future-masking as a zero-shot world-model probe, the surprise metric, the kinematic baseline in the matched latent metric, and the source-disjoint retraining protocol. P3 (Results): latent future prediction vs the infilling ceiling (E1), surprise-by-condition under source grouping with missingness/provenance controls (E2), and the kinematic baseline head-to-head (E3) — including any null outcomes. P4 (Generalization + rollouts): source-disjoint retraining pilot (E4) with the transductive-vs-held-out gap, and the autoregressive rollout / goal-conditioning feasibility (E5). P5 (Discussion): what a latent 'world model of the body' can and cannot honestly claim; the predictive-processing/active-inference link; the path to assistive-robotics and neurorehabilitation closed loops (predictive surprise as a feedback signal, goal/action conditioning); limitations (transductive, provenance, small N, single seed) and next steps toward a causal action-conditioned JEPA.
recommendation: Strong GO — this is the single most venue-aligned reframe available to the project (motor side of the loop, embodied AI, world models, SSL for biosignals, interpretability). It is runnable today on existing frozen checkpoints with no new training for the headline results, it produces a publishable contribution in BOTH the positive (latent forward dynamics emerge from infilling) and negative (infilling ≠ forecasting, a sharp boundary the JEPA-as-world-model literature assumes away) cases, and the only added cost — the source-disjoint retrain (~20 min) that converts a transductive observation into a valid generalization pilot — fits comfortably inside the 3-day deadline. Recommend committing to it as the D1 submission and pre-registering the surprise metric (h=4, cosine) before running E1–E3.
